note: A sound rendering of the avayavin discussion; one double negation is collapsed into its opposite.

errors.english: The phrase "for those who are not ill"
errors.why: The lemma is 'for the sick' (na ba rnams la), glossed as those struck by illness.

errors.english: Some possess no permission at all.
errors.why: This reports that some authorities do not admit the 'use by permission' category, not that some persons lack permission.

errors.english: Utilization by a master [note: of the teachings]
errors.why: bdag po'i yongs su longs spyod is use as an owner (svāmiparibhoga); the note about mastery of the teachings is misleading.

note: Generally follows the Vinaya lists; one negation was added that inverts the lemma for the sick, and the five kinds of use are glossed loosely.

errors.english: If one subdues the Mara demon of passions and practices restraint, what downfall could there be?
errors.why: The quoted case asks which offence a monk incurs who presses and holds back the emission (answer: sthūlātyaya); it is not about subduing Māra, and it is not rhetorical 'no downfall'.

errors.english: "what is applied to what has been done is not indeed undone,"
errors.why: The point is that it is not the case that no prayoga (deliberate application) was made; the English garbles the lemma and loses the prayoga term.

note: The Saṅghāvaśeṣa commentary is followed in outline, but the technical sense of prayoga (sbyor ba) and the quoted sthūlātyaya case are muddled.

errors.english: the head of (Indra) the king of the gods, here used in a logical syllogism
errors.why: śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is the stock Pramāṇa term for an anthill, which emits smoke-like vapour; the gloss misleads.

fix.find: the head of (Indra) the king of the gods, here used in a logical syllogism

note: The argument about the fire–smoke causal relation is followed well, except that the śakramūrdhan example is misexplained.

errors.english: the destruction of certain things is not an uncertain destruction

errors.english: is a inference of a pervading contradiction

errors.english: If one asks, "Why is destruction not initiated if that cause is absent?"
errors.why: The clause is the last reason inside the opponent's objection ('since without it destruction does not begin'), which ends at ཞེ་ན; it is not a separate question.

note: The argument about whether destruction has a cause is partly followed, but one conclusion is inverted, a named reason-type is mistranslated, and the objection is segmented wrongly.

errors.english: it does not function because of certainty
errors.why: The dark-son reason has the three modes yet does not operate to produce certainty, because avinābhāva is lacking.

errors.english: it is perceived as having its own identity in whatever way it may be
errors.why: This is a proof form: an entity or non-entity is of existent nature (probandum) because it is perceived in some way (reason). The English loses the thesis–reason structure.

errors.english: For example, even if there are three sons
errors.why: The whole side is verse (Pātrasvāmin's verses on anyathānupapatti) and is rendered as running prose.

note: The Trilakṣaṇakadarthana verses are rendered as prose, and the key point that the three modes do not yield certainty is inverted.

errors.why: gleng gzhi is Nidāna, not the Questions (Upāliparipṛcchā, zhus pa).

errors.english: a single momentary thing produces an effect that arises in that moment
errors.why: 'Occurring in a single moment' qualifies the thing that produces the effect (as the side later makes explicit), not the effect.

note: A faithful rendering of the argument from momentariness about solitary versus cooperative causes, including the variant reading.
